### Issue Summary

Sometimes internal server errors occur and the next server will respond with a `serverError: "Something went wrong while executing the operation."` (but still status code 200). Because of status 200 the frontend will not recognize it as an error and will still show a success toast (although something went wrong).
Formbricks should check the responses for a serverError when accessing backend functions:

```
if (result?.serverError) {
    throw new Error("Something went wrong");
}
```


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use eg #3301 to trigger an unsuccessful server only action
2. success toast will pop up although the operation actually failed

This happens in many places where the toast will pop up when there is no error during a server side action.

An error toast indicating the issue pops up (instead of falsely suggesting a successful operation)

We've built our documentation using [Nextra](https://nextra.site/docs). Right now, only Spanish and English are supported, but we would like to support more languages. 

This issue is for adding support for French.

## How to add support for a new language

The project is structured following [Nextra documentation](https://nextra.site/docs/docs-theme/start). There are a lot of files that have several versions of the same file (e.g. `introduction.en.mdx` and `introduction.es.mdx`). To add a new language, create a new version of every file (e.g. `introduction.fr.mdx`) and translate the content of the file using the English version as the base.

### Requirements
- The language name for French should be `fr`
- Include the new language in `locales` inside `next.config.js`
- All files must be translated (including `FAQ`)
- Spelling errors will not be accepted
- We prefer effective communication over a literal translation. Some concepts may be better to leave in English if the French translation doesn't make much sense in Opire's context

archive_tasks.issue_body_preview:
### Describe the bug

We're using Github (specifically a Github app) as an external IDP. We have configured Github to use expiring access tokens (good for 8 hours). When we want to get data from Github on behalf of the user, such as a list of repositories where the Github app is installed, we need a Github [user-to-server access token](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/installations#list-app-installations-accessible-to-the-user-access-token).

We can retrieve these external IDP tokens from keycloak via [this endpoint](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#retrieving-external-idp-tokens).

Unfortunately, if it has been more than 8 hours, then the access token is expired and the request to Github will fail. If I use the refresh token (which is also returned from the endpoint above), to get new tokens from Github, this works _once_. I get a new access and refresh token, and I can make a request to Github with the access token. However, this _expires_ the refresh token that Keycloak has. And there doesn't seem to be a way for me to give Keycloak the new access/refresh tokens that I've retrieved on behalf of the user.

Is this just an oversight? Is there any way to use Github as an external IDP with expiring access tokens?

### Version

19.0.2

### Expected behavior

1. Keycloak refreshes tokens _before_ returning them from `GET /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider_alias}/token` (provided the current `refresh_token` has not expired).

### Actual behavior

Keycloak appears to just return the exact response that it originally receives from Github, which is most likely an expired access token. If the refresh token is still good, it is worthless because using it will expire the one held in Keycloak.

### How to Reproduce?

Use Github as an external IDP with expiring tokens and try to use the endpoint as described above.

### Anything else?

_No response_

We've built our documentation using [Nextra](https://nextra.site/docs). Right now, only Spanish and English are supported, but we would like to support more languages. 

This issue is for adding support for French.

## How to add support for a new language

The project is structured following [Nextra documentation](https://nextra.site/docs/docs-theme/start). There are a lot of files that have several versions of the same file (e.g. `introduction.en.mdx` and `introduction.es.mdx`). To add a new language, create a new version of every file (e.g. `introduction.fr.mdx`) and translate the content of the file using the English version as the base.

### Requirements
- The language name for French should be `fr`
- Include the new language in `locales` inside `next.config.js`
- All files must be translated (including `FAQ`)
- Spelling errors will not be accepted
- We prefer effective communication over a literal translation. Some concepts may be better to leave in English if the French translation doesn't make much sense in Opire's context

history.issue_body_preview:
### Describe the bug

We're using Github (specifically a Github app) as an external IDP. We have configured Github to use expiring access tokens (good for 8 hours). When we want to get data from Github on behalf of the user, such as a list of repositories where the Github app is installed, we need a Github [user-to-server access token](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/apps/installations#list-app-installations-accessible-to-the-user-access-token).

We can retrieve these external IDP tokens from keycloak via [this endpoint](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#retrieving-external-idp-tokens).

Unfortunately, if it has been more than 8 hours, then the access token is expired and the request to Github will fail. If I use the refresh token (which is also returned from the endpoint above), to get new tokens from Github, this works _once_. I get a new access and refresh token, and I can make a request to Github with the access token. However, this _expires_ the refresh token that Keycloak has. And there doesn't seem to be a way for me to give Keycloak the new access/refresh tokens that I've retrieved on behalf of the user.

Is this just an oversight? Is there any way to use Github as an external IDP with expiring access tokens?

### Version

19.0.2

### Expected behavior

1. Keycloak refreshes tokens _before_ returning them from `GET /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider_alias}/token` (provided the current `refresh_token` has not expired).

### Actual behavior

Keycloak appears to just return the exact response that it originally receives from Github, which is most likely an expired access token. If the refresh token is still good, it is worthless because using it will expire the one held in Keycloak.

### How to Reproduce?

Use Github as an external IDP with expiring tokens and try to use the endpoint as described above.

### Anything else?
